extracted.intended_audience: candidates seeking to sit the Singapore Patent Agents Qualifying Examination (QE) 2026 / prospective Singapore patent agents
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative and exam syllabus instructions for candidates preparing for the Singapore Patent Agents Qualifying Examination (QE) 2026, covering enrolment, conduct, permitted materials, marking, grading, and detailed syllabus and assessment criteria for Papers A–D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Qualifying Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the Qualifying Examination is to assess whether the candidate is sufficiently proficient in the law of patents and has the necessary knowledge and practical experience to carry out patent agency work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examination (Papers A–D) is a statutory requirement before the Registrar proceeds to register an individual as a patent agent under the Patents Act and Patents (Patent Agents) Rules 2001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exam Structure (Papers A–D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Qualifying Examination comprises four Papers: Paper A: Preparation of a Patent Specification; Paper B: Amendment of a Patent Specification; Paper C: Infringement and Validity of Singapore Patent; Paper D: Knowledge of Patent Law and Patent Practice in Singapore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Annex A for a brief description and the syllabus for each Paper. Each Paper is 4 hours including reading time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites for Enrolment
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual must meet one of: (a) Passed the Graduate Certificate in Intellectual Property Law (GCIP) (NUS Faculty of Law); (b) Passed the corresponding modules under GDIPIM or MIPIM (SUSS) for the QE paper(s) they enroll in; or (c) Obtained Registrar's approval for exemption from passing GCIP/GDIPIM/MIPIM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates awaiting GDIPIM/MIPIM results when submitting the enrolment form must submit results by 26 December 2025 or their enrolment will be considered as not having been made. It is advisable to have completed at least one year of full-time training or internship in patent agency work before enrolling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrolment process, fees and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrolment requires a duly completed Enrolment Form with supporting documents, a non-refundable enrolment fee of $32.10 (inclusive of GST), and relevant examination fees. Closing date for enrolment is 19 September 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, applicants receive an email to make payment within 3 working days; only enrolments with full payment by the deadline are accepted. Fees are generally not refundable (see withdrawal/absence rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Index number and anonymity of answer scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: When full payment is made, the Examination Secretariat allocates each candidate a distinctive index number to be used in all communications and as the only identifier on answer scripts. Candidates must not indicate their names or initials on answer scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Examination Secretariat keeps names and index numbers confidential. Candidates found identifying themselves may be disqualified or suspended immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional enrolment for awaiting module results
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates awaiting GDIPIM/MIPIM results may receive provisional confirmation of enrolment but will be allowed to attempt papers only if they submit supporting documents showing they have passed the corresponding modules by 26 December 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supporting documents are not submitted by that date, enrolment for the relevant paper(s) will be considered not made and examination fees refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation on number of Papers per sitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are encouraged to sit only for the Paper(s) they are well prepared for; statistics indicate candidates who take up to two Papers at one sitting tend to have a higher passing rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is guidance (not a strict rule) intended to improve candidates' chances; consult Section B for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification or Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If candidates fail to comply with administrative instructions before or during the examination, or engage in plagiarism or cheating, the Examination Secretariat may disqualify or suspend them from the examination and inform the Examination Board as soon as feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates caught cheating will not be allowed to sit remaining Papers and will not be allowed to participate in subsequent examinations. No refund of examination fees will be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence, withdrawal, and refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate not present at the venue to sit for the Paper(s) will be considered absent. A candidate may request withdrawal and seek refund in writing with valid reasons and documentary evidence; the Registrar may allow or refuse withdrawal and any refund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawals should reach IPOS at least one week before the examination to be considered. Refunds will not be issued for withdrawal requests made during or after the examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading scheme and pass threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Paper is graded Pass (not less than 50% of the marks available) or Fail (less than 50%). Where disqualified/suspended/absent, Papers are graded Disqualified, Suspended, or Absent respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To pass the Qualifying Examination as required under the Patents (Patent Agents) Rules 2001, a candidate must obtain a pass grade for all Papers (Papers A to D). The candidate's mark range will be indicated in the Result Slip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking process and decision flow
rubrics_metrics.description: After the QE, the Examination Secretariat sends each answer script to two Primary Examiners for assessment. If Primaries disagree (Pass vs Fail), scripts return for reconsideration; persistent disagreement leads to referral to a Secondary Examiner. The Examination Committee's recommendations (with comments) are forwarded to the Examination Board, which deliberates and decides; the Board's decision is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full marking/deliberation/finalisation process takes approximately five months. Results are released by registered post and announced on www.ipos.gov.sg; cleaned answer scripts will be sent back to candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Result release timing and method
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying Examination results will be furnished to each candidate at the email address provided in the Enrolment Form; an official announcement of results will be published on the IPOS website (stated date: 26 June 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for hand delivery of results will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-sitting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates who have failed one or more Papers may apply to re-sit those Papers. There is no restriction on the number of attempts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Annex B for applicable examination fees for repeat attempts (fees increase from 4th attempt onwards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance, late arrival and leaving rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must confirm dates/venues and ensure timely arrival. Late arrivals will not be granted additional time; candidates arriving more than 30 minutes late may be denied entry. Candidates may leave for toilet breaks but may not take anything out; those who complete early may leave no earlier than 30 minutes after the start provided they have submitted their answer scripts; candidates are not allowed to leave during the last 30 minutes of the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates who leave early and submit cannot return to the room. Withdrawal requests must reach IPOS at least one week before the exam; withdrawals during or after the exam do not get refunds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation and postponement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examination Secretariat may discontinue and postpone the examination before or during the course of the examination due to unforeseeable circumstances (e.g., power failure, fire) with Registrar approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such decisions are taken for safety and integrity; further instructions will be provided to candidates as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of laptops (required and provided)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laptops will be provided by IPOS and their use is required for all candidates. Candidates preferring to write instead must submit a laptop opt-out request together with the Enrolment Form and documentary evidence; requests are considered case-by-case and, once approved, are final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a laptop has a technical issue during the exam, inform the Examination Secretariat immediately; if unresolved, a replacement laptop will be provided for the remainder of the exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination materials supplied on laptops and in room
rubrics_metrics.description: Each candidate will be supplied: (a) a single laptop; (b) a softcopy of the relevant examination paper in English; (c) a softcopy of the Singapore Patents Act and Rules; (d) a blank softcopy answer script; (e) a hardcopy of the Question Paper; (f) any other soft/hardcopy documents required to be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should ensure they can view the paper and type answers in the provided answer script; candidates may bring a personal keyboard/mouse/extra clothing if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typing and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must type answers in the fixed format provided, answer in English only, type their given index number on the header of the answer scripts, save work regularly, and follow end-of-exam steps: stop typing when time is up, type 'This is the last page' at the end, ensure no blank pages, save final work, and confirm submission with invigilator(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates who do not follow submission protocol risk their answers not being accepted. Regular saving is strongly encouraged (e.g., every 10–20 minutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted hardcopy Reference Materials (and cutoff date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may bring hardcopies of: Singapore statutory provisions (Patents Act (Cap.221); Patents Rules; Patents (Patent Agents) Rules 2001; Patents (Composition of Offences) Regulations 2001), Paris Convention, Budapest Treaty, PCT and PCT Regulations, latest lists of members to WTO/Budapest/Paris/PCT, decisions relevant to Patents Law as decided by Singapore Courts (dated before 30 June 2025), and language/technical dictionaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to Acts/Rules/Regulations/Treaties include corresponding amendments implemented before 30 June 2025. The 'latest list of members' is taken as of 30 June 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation and cross-referencing rules for Reference Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotations in Reference Materials are not allowed. Cross-referencing and highlighting are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition and examples provided: 'Annotate' = supply with critical/explanatory notes (e.g., noting prescribed fees/forms/time) — prohibited. 'Cross-referencing' = noting page numbers, relevant Sections or Rules without further explanatory notes — permitted. Invigilators will check and may confiscate materials that do not satisfy these conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited items and conduct in the exam room
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are NOT permitted to have electronic/portable storage devices (tablets, personal laptops, mobile phones, flash drives, portable hard drives, PDAs, alarm clocks, related devices), other reading materials than allowed Reference Materials, to look at the Paper before commencement (unless instructed), to cheat or attempt to cheat, to communicate with one another after the start and before the end of the examination, to smoke, to behave in a disorderly manner, or to leave the room without invigilator consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All prohibited devices are to be placed out of reach as indicated by the invigilator. Invigilators may remove/confiscate disallowed items or materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct expectations and seat/belongings rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are requested to occupy their allocated seat throughout the exam unless advised otherwise, place belongings as indicated by invigilator, and ensure no belongings are left behind after leaving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules help maintain order and exam integrity; failure to comply may result in disciplinary action including disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and handling of candidate identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examination Secretariat has custody of and will keep in confidence the names and the index numbers of the candidates. The index number alone is to be the identifier on answer scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the index number in all communications; disclosing identity on scripts may lead to disqualification or suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper A syllabus: Specification drafting substantive criteria and marks allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper A requires drafting a specification for filing in Singapore that complies with the Patents Act and Patents Rules. The specification must (a) disclose the invention in a manner clear and complete for a person skilled in the art to perform the invention; and (b) include claims that (i) define the matter for which protection is sought; (ii) are clear and concise; (iii) are supported by the description; (iv) relate to one invention or a group linked as a single inventive concept; (v) have at least one independent claim offering the broadest possible protection and being novel, inventive and industrially applicable; and (vi) include dependent claims for fallback positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time allowed: 4 hours including reading time. Broad allocation of marks: Independent Claim(s) 50–60 marks; Dependent Claims 20–30 marks; Description 20 marks. References include specific sections of the Patents Act and Patents Rules (listed in Annex A). Candidates are to assume receiving a client letter and pertinent prior art when drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper B syllabus: Amendment tasks, assumptions and marks allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper B tests amendment of a patent specification: candidates may be required to review the client's reply and draft a response to a Written Opinion (including prior art analysis & argument), provide amended claims and the basis for amendments, and draft a client advice letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time allowed: 4 hours including reading time. Broad allocation of marks: Draft response to Written Opinion 35 marks; Claim Amendments 35 marks; Client Advice Letter 30 marks. Candidates must accept facts given, assume prior art provided is exhaustive, not use special knowledge, and in some situations may not need to amend the description. Relevant Patents Act/Rules and case law references are provided in Annex A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper C syllabus: Infringement and validity advisory criteria and marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper C requires advice on infringement and validity of a Singapore patent: claim construction, infringement analysis, validity (including internal validity issues such as sufficiency), and drafting a letter to the client. Candidates must advise on how the patent may be amended to improve the patentee's position and the impact of amendments on prior advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time allowed: 4 hours including reading time. Broad allocation of marks: Claim Construction 35 marks; Infringement 25 marks; Validity 25 marks; Letter 15 marks. Advice must give clear, logical reasons, cite and apply relevant laws and cases. Candidates must accept facts and provided prior art as exhaustive. Extensive Singapore case law and some UK authorities are listed as references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper D syllabus: Knowledge of Patent Law & Practice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper D requires candidates to display a thorough and practical knowledge of Patents Law and Practice in Singapore, covering topics such as pre/post grant prosecution in Singapore, patentability requirements, rights to a patent, who is an inventor, amendments, infringement proceedings, revocation proceedings, international applications and treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time allowed: 4 hours including reading time. Allocation: Five questions to be answered, maximum 20 marks each. Answers should be brief, to the point, and supported by sections, rules or other legal basis where relevant. Candidates should note recent changes in the Patents Act and Rules incorporated before 30 June 2025. References include Patents Act, Patents Rules, Patents (Patent Agents) Rules 2001, PCT, Paris, Budapest, WTO lists, and Singapore decisions dated before 30 June 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of facts and prior art in Papers B and C
rubrics_metrics.description: For Papers B and C, candidates are to accept the facts given in the Paper and not use any special knowledge they may have. They are to assume that the prior art provided is exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This instruction limits candidates to the materials supplied in the question and ensures fairness; external knowledge beyond what is provided should not be used unless explicitly permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples/definitions and permitted interpretation aids
rubrics_metrics.description: The instructions provide definitions and examples (e.g., definition of 'annotate' and what counts as annotation vs cross-referencing; examples of case law that may be relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples clarify permitted behaviors (e.g., cross-referencing allowed) and the scope of reference materials and legal sources candidates may rely upon during the exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees structure and tiered attempt pricing (Annex B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrolment fee: $32.10 (inclusive of GST). Examination Fee: First to third attempt $642 per paper (inclusive of GST); fourth and subsequent attempts $1,284 per paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 2 fees apply based on number of attempts of each QE paper from QE 2022 onwards. Examples illustrate cumulative attempts across years and how fees apply when attempting multiple papers in same QE year.
